findings.title: S3 bucket with public ACL
findings.description: Bucket ACLs granting public-read, public-read-write, or authenticated-read expose objects beyond the account.
findings.remediation:
Remove the public ACL grant. Set the bucket ACL to private and rely on bucket
policies for access control:
resource "aws_s3_bucket_acl" "this" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.this.id
  acl    = "private"
}
Then enable all four public-access-block settings (see AEGIS-AWS-003 fix).

findings.title: Security group ingress open to the world
findings.description: Ingress rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 expose the workload to the entire internet. Restrict source CIDRs to known ranges.
findings.remediation:
Restrict the ingress CIDR to trusted ranges. Replace `0.0.0.0/0` with your
office/VPN CIDRs, or remove the rule and use SSM Session Manager (no inbound
SSH needed):
ingress {
  from_port   = 22
  to_port     = 22
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["203.0.113.0/24"]  # your trusted range
}

findings.title: Security group egress open to the world

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in resource config
findings.description: A database password written as a literal in Terraform config is stored in state, plan output, and version control. The same holds for a secret-like variable or local flowing into a credential attribute. Reference a secrets manager or a generated password instead. The secret value is never included in findings.

evidence.expected: reference to a secrets manager or generated password

findings.remediation:
Remove the hardcoded credential and rotate it immediately — it is compromised.
Reference a Secrets Manager secret instead:
data "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "db" {
  secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.db.id
}
# then: password = jsondecode(data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db.secret_string)["password"]

findings.description: The policy combines a policy-authoring action (iam:CreatePolicy, iam:PutRolePolicy, iam:PutUserPolicy, iam:PutGroupPolicy) with a policy-attachment action (iam:AttachRolePolicy, iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:AttachGroupPolicy). evidence.expected: separate policy authoring from attachment; scope both to least privilege

findings.remediation:
Split policy authoring from attachment (this combination is the classic privilege
escalation primitive). Remove `iam:CreatePolicy*` / `iam:Attach*Policy` from the

never in an application runtime role.

Attack path: launch a compute resource passing an administrative role, then steal its credentials from the instance metadata / environment. Scope iam:PassRole to specific role ARNs.

evidence.actual: Allow statements grant iam:PassRole on "*" with a compute-launch primitive
evidence.expected: scope iam:PassRole to specific role ARNs

findings.remediation:
Scope `iam:PassRole` to the exact role ARNs the workload must pass, and only
together with the specific compute-launch action it needs:

  "Action": "iam:PassRole",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AppExecutionRole"
}
Never grant `iam:PassRole` on `*` — it lets the holder escalate to any role.

findings.description: A secret with no description is unidentifiable in audits and secret inventories. Describe the secret's purpose and owner.
findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

findings.title: Backup vault without vault lock configuration
findings.description: A Backup vault with no aws_backup_vault_lock_configuration allows recovery points to be deleted before their retention period expires, undermining ransomware protection. Add a vault lock in compliance mode with a minimum retention.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: ALB listener with an outdated SSL policy
findings.description: An ALB listener whose ssl_policy references a 2016-era or TLS-1-0 policy negotiates weak ciphers and obsolete TLS versions. Use a current ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13 policy.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: API Gateway method without a request validator
findings.description: An API Gateway method with no request_validator_id accepts unvalidated request bodies and parameters, pushing malformed input into the backend. Attach a request validator enforcing body and parameter validation.
